## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
Empty criteria now count as proven: the rewrite of `requirement_proven` makes an empty criteria list return `True`, so the release-review gate passes requirements it used to reject. The pull request says no behavior change is intended, so this needs fixing before merge.

## Changes
The pull request replaces `typing.List`/`Dict` with built-in generics and `Logger.warn` with `Logger.warning` across 180 handler modules. It switches `by_name` to `operator.itemgetter`, rewrites the proof count in `requirement_proven`, and adds a one-line `review.txt`.

## Critical
- app/handlers/h091_requirements.py:12 — correctness — Return False for an empty criteria list — With `criteria=[]`, `sum(...)` is `0` and `len(criteria)` is `0`, so `proven == len(criteria)` returns `True`. The removed `bool(criteria) and all(...)` returned `False`, and line 10 still warns "requirement has no criteria" before the call reports the requirement as proven. — Release review treats a requirement with no criteria as proven, which contradicts the stated "No behavior change is intended." — Fix: Restore `bool(criteria) and all(item["proven"] for item in criteria)`, and add an empty-list case to `test_requirement_proof` in `tests/test_handlers.py`, which currently has none.
